Q: How can I convert an HTML document to a Microsoft Word .docx document in Python? A:

In Windows, the easiest way will be to use MS Word using the pywin32 plugin. Here is good answer with example code.

Using pypandoc:

output = pypandoc.convert(source='/path/to/file.html', format='html', to='docx', outputfile='/path/to/output.docx', extra_args=['-RTS'])

Read this for extra_args.

Q: Assigning a zsh array via a nameref A: 
set -A $name one two ...

or

read -A $name <<<"one two ..."
# or any input redirection with suitable contents

which is uglier but can be generalized like e.g.

IFS=$'\n' read -d '' -A $name < <(echo one really; grep -m1 this that; sed -n $((foo*3))p <other)

(although because NL is separator here not terminator, 'normal' text which ends with a NL will leave the last array element empty; you may want to delete it).

Q: Best practice for updating nested resume data in PostgreSQL: delete-and-reinsert vs differential updates? A:

It depends on

  • the number of rows for each user

  • the expected number of resume updates per minute

If you end up deleting and re-inserting not too many rows, PostgreSQL and autovacuum will be able to cope, and you can keep it simple. If the load is more serious, it is probably a good idea to invest the effort to minimize the data churn.

Q: How can numpy be so much faster than my Fortran routine? A:

In the future, when you are working with large data.... A LOT. I mean working with this data size ten thousand times.

Assumptions

  1. Workstation level hardware

Suggestion

  1. Move data to NVMe.

  2. Do OpenMP at a large level at the outer loop, where each thread works on one file at a time. Today's NVME should be able to read 2-10 files per second. If you have like 10 - 32. Such reading is fine. If you have >32 cores, then pause once in a while.

  3. If you have more core than that. Split to several groups and let each group do parallel sum by splitting the outer array e.g. i-indices if you data is DATA(k, j, i). The number of parallel read should be kept below 20. OpenMP requires minimal effort to learn and implement. So it would not hurt to try.

  4. There is no need to do a parallel read of a file if your data is not in the terabyte regime. 10GB via stream read is done in a snap (slow snap, albeit). And if your data is not stored on parallel disks that can provide more than 5GB per thread, there is absolutely no need for that.

  5. If you really care for accuracy and the "true" mean. Maybe you need to sort the data. This will be painful, but imagine if you have 128^3 of 1E-6, and 128^3 of 1E8. If I sum across groups one and two, I may get a completely different result than finding the mean of each group and weighting them. Maybe using quadruple precision would be faster than sorting.

  6. Maybe you should consider using HDF5 if you are working with large data. Parallel I/O, and parallel data operation and statistics are already implemented.

Q: IndexError: list index out of range in Python - how to capture the last item in a list? A:

you can try using my_list[-1]
it is called list slicing where -1 means last element of the array and -2 means second last.
